analysis: The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md. The patch (new hunk lines 1-16) adds an "Unreleased — Gemma 4 MLXFast opt-in ports" section describing opt-in decode/prefill, expert-routing and cache fast-paths, and MTP evidence handling. It claims optimization flags are off by default and that prefix-cache policy, model weights, quantization, batching and paging are preserved. It also states that a known longer fixed-L4/B8 MTP parity failure remains visible and that release readiness is not established. Modes are unchanged at 100644. There is no executable code, configuration, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or data-exposure change in the supplied diff. The changelog's claims about cache policy being unchanged relate to T-041 (prefix-cache and TTFT oracle, A-001). They cannot be verified here because the Gemma 4 and MLXFast source files are not supplied. The threat model's T-041 text names Gemma 4 for long-context SSD caching, with an adoption bound of 25,600 tokens and a per-donation gate. A later pass that sees the actual provider-swift Gemma 4 or cache code should confirm that the fast-path ports do not alter the SSD cache salt scoping, HMAC lookup tags, TTL or donation gate, and do not change the coordinator-plaintext assumptions. The "seed-only automatic-cap fallback" and MTP evidence-separation notes refer to code outside this batch. Coverage limit: only documentation was reviewed. No threat-model update is required from this PR alone.
